Synergy: If your BAB is at least +6 and you also have the Combat Reflexes feat, whenever an opponent with effective reach of 0 ft. against you attempts an attack of opportunity against another character, you can spend one of your own attacks of opportunity to automatically negate the attempt.
Source: This stance supersedes the Titan Mauler’s variant class feature of the same nameUC, and also the Elusive StanceDr333 and Running CirclesCBEM feats, and the covering strike maneuverToB.

sections.heading: Exhausting DefenseDr345 [Skill, Stance]
sections.text:
You coax your opponents into wasting their strength.
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +6, Dodge, Endurance 1 rank.
Benefit: Designate one foe per round as the target of this feat. The target must succeed at a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half your base attack bonus + your Constitution modifier) each round when attacking you in melee or suffer 1d6 nonlethal damage (+1d6 per 4 points of your BAB, to a maximum of 6d6 at BAB +20). The target suffers this damage a maximum of once per round, no matter how many times you are attacked.
If your base attack bonus is +6 or greater and you have 6 or more ranks in Endurance, an opponent failing the save is also fatigued, even if not damaged to below half its normal hp.If your base attack bonus is +11 or greater and you have 11 or more ranks in Endurance, if already fatigued, an opponent failing the save becomes exhausted.
Synergy: You can use this stance in conjunction with Combat Expertise; this is a specific exception to the non-stacking rule for stances. If you use Combat Expertise against a fatigued or exhausted foe for 1 round, then attack the next round without using Combat Expertise, your opponent is flat-footed for 1 round and you gain an additional +2 circumstance bonus to attack him until your next turn.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Armiger’s “draining defense” class featureIH.

sections.heading: Expertise, Combat [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As described in Chapter 7 (Combat), this feat improves your ability to fight defensively, as shown in the table below.
Base Attack Bonus | Attack Penalty | Defensive Fighting | Total Defense
+1 to +3 | -1 | +2 | +3
+4 to +7 | -2 | +4 | +6
+8 to +11 | -3 | +6 | +9
+12 to +15 | -4 | +8 | +12
+16 to +19 | -5 | +10 | +15
+20 | -6 | +12 | +18
Synergy: If you also have the Vital Strike and Weapon Finesse feats, when in this stance and fighting defensively or using total defense, you apply your Vital Strike damage to any melee attack you make with a finesse weapon, even if the normal activating conditions have not been met. This supersedes the Deadly Defense featCSc.
Normal: The dodge bonus to AC while fighting defensively is 1:1 with the penalty to attacks, or 2:1 when using total defense.
Note: In essence, this feat doubles the effectiveness of fighting defensively, and should logically be renamed Improved Defensive Fighting. The name “Combat Expertise” is retained for the convenience of interaction with 3.5 and Pathfinder rules that reference this feat.

sections.heading: Flanking, AdaptablePHII [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Combat Reflexes, Improved Flanking.
Benefit: Each round, designate a single opponent as the target of this feat. When the chosen target is within your reach, you can provide Aid Another bonuses to allies’ attacks against it as a free action, and you can choose to count as occupying your square or any square you threaten for purposes of determining whether you can provide or receive flanking bonuses with allies.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, the designated opponent is always treated as flanked by all opponents adjacent to it, even if they do not spend immediate actions. If your BAB is +11 or higher, the effects of this feat apply to all adjacent opponents.If your BAB is +16 or higher, the effects of this feat apply to all opponents within your reach.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Superior Flanking featCBEM; the Dedicated Nuisance featDr343; the Gang Up featAPG; the Polearm Master’s “flexible flanker” variant class featureAPG; and the Swordsage’s island of blades stanceToB.

sections.heading: Giant’s StanceToB [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Power Attack.
Benefit: As a swift action, you can adopt a stance allowing you to put extra leverage into your blows. As long as you remain in this stance, you deal damage in melee as if any weapon you wield (or any unarmed attack) was one size greater than actual. You gain no size modifiers; only base damage changes.
Special: Instead of simply increasing a normal weapon’s base damage, you can instead use this feat to wield a weapon one size larger than you could normally use.

sections.heading: Hold the LineCW [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Dodge.
Benefit: While in this stance, you get a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class against charge attacks; this bonus improves by +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus (maximum +6 at BAB +20). This bonus also applies to your CMB when attempting a Counter Charge maneuver (Chapter 1).
If your BAB is +6 or higher, any opponent who misses you with a charge attack provokes an attack of opportunity from you. If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can also make an attack of opportunity against any charging opponent who enters the area you threaten, even if you are not targeted. This attack of opportunity happens immediately before the charge attack is resolved. If you use a weapon with the brace property, this attack deals double damage as if you had set it to receive the charge.
Special: This feat does not grant you more attacks of opportunity than you are normally allowed in a round. If you are flat-footed or otherwise denied your Dexterity bonus to Armor Class, you do not gain the benefit of this feat.
Normal: You only get an attack of opportunity against a character that exits a square you threaten.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Sidestep Charge featSRD; the Phalanx Fighter’s “ready pike” class featureAPG; and the Resist Charge featCBEM.

sections.heading: Iron GuardToB [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: While you are in this stance, any opponent that you threaten takes a –4 penalty on attack rolls against your allies (this penalty increases to -5 if your BAB is +6 or higher, to -6 at BAB +11, and to -17 at BAB +16). This penalty does not apply to attacks made against you. Enemies you threaten gain a passive Knowledge (warfare) check (Chapter 4) to become aware of the consequences of the stance.

sections.heading: Lunge [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: When you adopt this stance, you increase the reach of your melee attacks by 5 feet by taking a ­2 penalty to your AC until your next turn. You can return to a normal stance (using your standard reach) as a free action.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can activate this feat as a swift action.If your BAB is +11 or higher, you do not suffer the penalty to AC.If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can activate and de-activate this stance as a free action (i.e., it is no longer a stance, but a simple choice you make each time you attack).
Source: This stance also supersedes the Lunging Strike featPHII.

sections.heading: Martial SpiritToB [Stance]
sections.text: Benefit: While you are in this stance, each time you successfully damage an opponent that represents a credible threat (as defined under Combat Feats, above) with a melee attack, you or an ally within 30 feet (your choice with each hit) heals 2 points of damage (multiplied on a successful crit). This healing represents the vigor, drive, and toughness you inspire.

sections.heading: Menacing StanceUC [Skill, Stance]
sections.text:
While in this stance, you constantly harry and distract your enemies, causing them to make mistakes.
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +6, Bluff 6 ranks, Staredown.
Benefit: As long as you have at least one immediate action available, all enemies adjacent to you are automatically shaken (unless immune to that condition).
If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, enemies within your reach are unnerved instead (Chapter 7).If your BAB is +16 or higher and you have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, enemies within reach take a -2 penalty to saving throws/opposed checks against your frightful presence ability (from the Staredown feat).

sections.heading: Mystic Phoenix StanceToB [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +6, able to cast arcane spells, Arcane Boost.
Benefit: While in this stance, you gain a +2 dodge bonus to AC and to Concentration checks to cast defensively during any round in which you cast a spell or attempt to cast a spell or use a spell-like ability. In addition, when you activate your Arcane Boost ability, the effects of that feat last for as long as you maintain this stance (maximum 1 round per level of the spell expended).

sections.heading: Opportunist, PairedAPG [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: Whenever you are in this stance and adjacent to at least one ally, enemies that provoke attacks of opportunity from your ally also provoke attacks of opportunity from you so long as you threaten them (even if the situation or an ability would normally deny you the attack of opportunity). This does not allow you to take more than one attack of opportunity against a creature for a given action.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, the ally need not be adjacent, but merely within your reach.If your BAB is +11 or higher, whenever an ally successfully feints against an opponent, that opponent provokes an attack of opportunity from you.If your BAB is +16 or higher, once per round you can make an attack of opportunity against any opponent who has just been struck for damage in melee.
Synergy: If your BAB is at least +6 and you also have the Pont-Blank Shot feat, when an ally makes a ranged attack and hits an opponent within point-blank range of you, you can make a single ranged attack of opportunity against that opponent as an immediate action. Your ranged weapon must be in hand, loaded, and ready to be fired or thrown for you to make the ranged attack.
Source: This stance also supersedes the Ranged Opportunist featUC and the rogue’s “opportunist” talent.
Punishing StanceToB [Stance]
Benefit: While you are in this stance, you deal an extra 1d6 points of precision damage (Chapter 7) with all attacks. You also take a -2 penalty to AC, because this fighting stance emphasizes power over a defensive posture. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, you can increase the bonus damage by an additional +1d6 by increasing the AC penalty by an additional -2 (maximum +6d6 damage, -12 to AC at BAB +20).

sections.heading: Redirection [Stance]
sections.text:
You can adopt a stance allowing you to use an opponent’s power against him.
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Martial Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks), Improved Bull Rush or Improved Trip, Power Attack.
Benefit: As an immediate action, you can attempt a reposition or trip combat maneuver against an opponent who charges you, who attempts a forcing maneuver against you (Chapter 7), or who attacks you using the Power Attack feat. If successful, the attack is foiled and the attacker is sickened for 1 round, plus an additional round per 4 points of your base attack bonus. A Reflex save (DC = 10 + half your BAB + your Wisdom modifier) applies to halve the duration.
You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on the combat maneuver check and to the save DC for the redirection if the attacker is charging you or attempting a forcing maneuver against you. If the opponent is using Power Attack, these bonuses are instead equal to the penalty to attacks from the opponent’s Power Attack. If the opponent uses Power Attack on a charge, the bonuses stack (this is a specific exception to the non-stacking rule for like-named bonuses).
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can use this ability in response to one of the listed attack forms against an adjacent ally. If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can use redirection against any opponent that attacks you in melee, even that opponent is not using one of the listed attack forms. If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can use redirection in response to any melee attack against an adjacent ally.
Synergy: If you have both the Improved Bull Rush and Improved Trip feats, you can make both a reposition and a trip maneuver as part of a single immediate action with this ability.
Special: This feat allows you to qualify for the Manticore Parry fighter talent (q.v.) as if it were a feat, provided you meet the other prerequisites and your base attack bonus is +11 or higher. This simulates the Elusive Redirection featUC.
Source: This feat supersedes the Flowing Monk’s variant class feature of the same nameUC.

sections.heading: Sand DancerSSt [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Favored terrain (deserts), Improved Trip.
Benefit: If you successfully trip an opponent in any area of ash, dust, loose earth, or sand that is at least 1 inch deep, that opponent must take a full-round action to stand during the round after being tripped. Following that round, the target can get to his feet with a move action (as normal). The opponent still provokes attacks of opportunity while attempting to stand, as normal.
If your BAB is at least +6, in an area covered in a layer of at least 1 inch of ash, dust, loose earth, or sand, as an immediate action you can supplement an attack made in that same round with flung or kicked material. A foe damaged by your attack is blinded 1 round (Fortitude negates; DC 10 + half your base attack bonus + your Dex modifier). If your BAB is at least +11, the blinding spray of sand affects either a 5-ft. cone or a 5-ft. burst, at your option.
Special: Equivalent feats for different impeding conditions in other favored terrains might be allowed: Forest Dancer (undergrowth), Mountain Dancer (scree), etc.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Sandspinner and Sand Snare featsSSt

sections.heading: Shared ShieldCBEM [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As long as you have at least one immediate action available, when you fight defensively, you can apply that bonus to AC as a shield bonus to the AC of one ally you designate within your reach (you gain no AC bonus yourself, in this case).
If you are actively using a shield, you can instead simply choose to provide the AC bonus gained from your shield to one adjacent ally who does not have a shield (this does not require an action on your part), or share half this bonus with all adjacent allies. When using this function, as an immediate action, you can increase your shield bonus by +4; this supersedes the Crusader’ shield block counterToB.
Synergy:
Improvements to fighting defensively (such as Combat Expertise) can also be applied when using this feat to protect one ally; this is a specific exception to general rule of non-stacking of [stance] effects. If your BAB is +6 or higher, when you fight defensively or use the total defense option, the full AC bonus you receive extends to all allies in adjacent squares as well, as long as you retain at least one unused immediate action. If you use the Combat Expertise feat, you receive the full benefit, and adjacent allies receive the normal fighting defensively bonus (+1, +1 per 4 points of your BAB) in addition to the shield bonus.You can use this feat in conjunction with the Two-Weapon Defense feat. When this is done with a polearm, the effect is similar to the Polearm Master’s polearm parryAPG.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Covering Defense and Saving Shield feats and Phalanx Fighter’s “shield ally” variant class featureAPG, the Cavalier’s “champion” class featureCH, and the Knight Protector’s defensive stanceCW.

sections.heading: Shield WallAPG [Stance]
sections.text:
You are skilled at positioning yourself together with those around you for greater protection.
Prerequisite: Shield Proficiency.
Benefit: Whenever you are wielding a shield and are adjacent to an ally who is doing likewise, the AC bonus from your shields increases. If an adjacent ally is wielding a light shield, your shield bonus increases by +1; if your ally is wielding a heavy shield, your shield bonus increases by +2. If your ally is wielding a tower shield, your shield bonus increases by +3; if the ally instead uses the tower shield to gain total cover, you also benefit if an attack targeting you passes through the edge of the shield (CRB, p. 153).

sections.heading: Snake StyleUC [Skill, Stance]
sections.text:
You watch your foe’s every movement and then punch through its defense.
Prerequisites: Bluff 1 rank, Combat Reflexes, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks), Improved Feint.
Benefit: While in this stance, your baffling defense (see Improved Feint) is always active; you can use 10 + your Bluff bonus in place of your normal AC. Your CMB in this stance is equal to 10 + your Bluff modifier + your Strength modifier + your size modifier + any bonuses from Improved Maneuvers feats.
If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff, whenever you score a critical threat with an unarmed attack while in this stance, you can make a Bluff check in place of the attack roll to confirm the critical hit. Whenever you confirm a critical hit with your unarmed attack, you can spend an immediate action to take a 5-foot step even if you have otherwise moved this round; this step does not end your stance.If you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, when an opponent’s attack misses you while you are using this stance (i.e., fails to meet your Bluff results), you can make an unarmed attack against that opponent as an attack of opportunity (assuming you have at least immediate action remaining that round, after the one you used for your AC).If you have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, if you make an unarmed attack of opportunity in response to a miss and you score a hit, you can make another attack of opportunity against the same opponent (assuming you have at least one immediate action left after using the other two with this feat).

sections.heading: Stance Mastery [Combat]
sections.text:
You can maintain stances when others cannot.
Prerequisites: BAB +6; any stance feat or talent.
Benefit: While in a stance that normally ends if you move, you can move 5 ft. (or take a 5-ft. step) and still maintain the effects of the stance. If you remain immobile, you can instead choose to maintain the effects of two stances simultaneously.
If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can move up to 10 feet and still maintain the stance.If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can move up to half your normal speed and still maintain the stance.
Source: This feat supersedes the Warblade class feature of the same nameToB, and also the Stalwart Defender’s mobile stanceAPG and the Master of Many Styles’ perfect styleUC.

sections.heading: Steadfast PikeAPG [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Martial Weapon Proficiency (pole-arms or spears).
Benefit: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus on attack rolls with readied attacks and attacks of opportunity made with a spear or polearm with which you have at least Martial proficiency. The bonus increases by +1 for every four points of your base attack bonus (maximum +6 at BAB +20).
Synergy: If you also have Exotic proficiency with a polearm or spear with the “brace” property, you deal triple damage against charging opponents, rather than double damage, when set to receive a charge. Alternatively, when set to receive a charge from a mounted opponent, you can brace your weapon and deal double damage to the mount and normal damage to the rider if you hit the mount.

sections.heading: Steady Stance [Stance]
sections.text: Benefit: While in this stance, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your Combat Maneuver Defense. This bonus increases by an additional +1 per 4 points of your base attack bonus.

sections.heading: Vigilant Defender [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: Each round you are in this stance, select one adjacent ally. Attacks made against that ally provoke attacks of opportunity from you. These attacks of opportunity are made with a morale bonus equal to one-fourth of your base attack bonus (maximum +5 at BAB +20).
If your BAB is at least +6, the ally need not be adjacent, as long as he or she is within reach.If your BAB is at least +11, you can defend two adjacent allies.If your BAB is at least +16, you can defend two allies within reach, or on any number of adjacent allies.
Source: This feat supersedes the Devoted Defender’s defensive strikeS&F and the Knight Protector’s retributive attackCW class features.

sections.heading: Wind Stance [Stance]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +1, Dodge.
Benefit: If you move more than 5 feet, you gain a 5% miss chance (treat as due to concealment) for 1 round. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, the miss chance increases by 5% (maximum 30% at BAB +20). Against ranged attacks, the miss chance is doubled (10% at BAB +1, maximum 60% at BAB +20).
Special: This stance is a specific exception to the general rule of non-mobility for stances; rather, it requires movement in order to operate.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Lightning Stance feat, and the Swordsage’s child of shadow stanceToB.

sections.heading: Combat Feats, Strikes
sections.text:
Strikes are a special subset of combat feats that add additional effects to your attacks, but generally at the cost of being able to make only one attack that round. Unless otherwise noted, Strikes that require an attack as a standard action can also be used in conjunction with a single attack at the end of a charge, or a single attack made using the Spring Attack feat.
Immunity: Except where noted or when obviously not applicable, strikes are considered [precision] effects (Chapter 7). They are therefore ineffective against creatures that are immune to critical hits or precision damage (this includes opponents that do not have a discernible anatomy, although this latter condition is waived if you have oozes as a favored enemy—see Ranger).
Saving Throws: Many Strikes allow a saving throw to mitigate the effects. Unless otherwise noted, the save DC for melee and thrown weapon strikes is equal to 10 + half your base attack bonus + your Strength modifier. If you have the Weapon Finesse feat and execute a Strike, you can instead choose to set the DC as 10 + half your BAB + your Dexterity modifier. For strikes made with projectile weapons, calculate the save DC using your Wisdom modifier instead,
For strikes that activate on a critical and allow a saving throw, add +2 to the save DC for weapons with a x3 critical multiplier, and +4 to the save DC for weapons with a x4 critical multiplier.
Synergy: The effects of most strikes can be automatically applied to certain other attacks, depending on the prerequisites met:
To a single attack of opportunity if you have the Combat Reflexes feat;To a confirmed critical hit if you have the Improved Critical feat;To a pin if you have the Improved Grapple feat; To a successful sneak attack.
Special: Unless you have the Striking Mastery fighter talent (q.v.), the effects of only one strike can be added to any given attack.
All [Strike] feats are also [Combat] feats, although the [Combat] descriptor is omitted in the titles.
Sources: Strike feats are meant to organize the various “critical” feats from the Pathfinder core rules, the “assault” featsAPG, and the martial strikesToB into a more or less unified mechanic.

sections.heading: Anchoring BlowDr306 [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +6.
Benefit: As a standard action, you can perform an anchoring blow. Any opponent damaged by that attack is also affected as if by a dimensional anchor spell (caster level equals your base attack bonus). There is no saving throw, but spell resistance applies normally.
If your BAB is +11 or higher, you gain the effects of a permanent dimensional anchor on yourself as well as an extraordinary ability. You can lower or reinstate it as a free action. While this ability is active, any creature you grapple is likewise automatically affected. If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can enter a stance that expands your dimensional anchor to an aura to encompass a 20-ft. emanation (as a dimensional lock spell). This effect has all the limitations standard to [Stance] feats.
Synergy: If you also have the planar tracking class feature (see Ranger), when a creature you are grappling attempts to dimension door, plane shift, teleport, or use any similar transportation effect, you immediately know the intended destination and can choose whether to apply your dimensional anchor effect, lower the effect and allow the effect as intended, or allow the effect and also “piggyback” along, as if you had no weight (for purposes of counting against the weight limit of effects like dimension door). This supersedes the Guardian’s Dimensional Grappler abilityMA.
Source: This feat also supersedes the Aura of Stability powerPnH.

sections.heading: Avalanche of BladesToB [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +11, Combat Reflexes.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If this attack hits, you may spend an immediate action to make a second attack against the same opponent, albeit at a –4 penalty. As long as you continue to hit the opponent, you can continue to make additional attacks against that same target, but each additional attack suffers an additional –4 penalty (-8 for the third attack, -12 for the fourth, -16 for the fifth, etc.). Any miss breaks the tempo and ends your chain of attacks.
Synergy: If you have the rogue’s “surprise attacks” class feature, you can activate the Avalanche of Blades feat whenever you successfully sneak attack an opponent during a surprise round. This supersedes the Hellcat Pounce featPC.

sections.heading: Baffling StrikeCBEM [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. Any opponent damaged by this attack also takes a circumstance penalty to attack rolls and damage equal to half your base attack bonus (round up), lasting until your next turn. This is a minor [debilitation] condition. The penalty does not multiply on a successful critical hit, but the duration does.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, on a failed Fortitude save the effects last for 1 round per point of your base attack bonus. This is a moderate [debilitation] condition.If your BAB is +11 or higher, on a failed save the effect lasts for 1 minute per point of your base attack bonus or until the wound that inflicted the effect is healed; it can also be removed by a restoration spell. This is a severe [debilitation] condition.If your BAB is +16 or higher, on a failed save the effect lasts until the target recovers its full normal hit points (through healing or rest); it can also be removed with greater restoration. This is a critical [debilitation] condition.
Source: This feat also supersedes the Rogue’s befuddling strike talentAPG and the Archer’s “distracting shot” token abilityIH.

sections.heading: Bleeding Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack with a slashing or piercing weapon that deals an additional 1d4 points of bleed damage per round, in addition to normal damage.
The amount of bleed damage increases with your base attack bonus, according to the following table:
 | Bleed Damage on a:
Base Attack | Standard Action | Full Attack
+1 to +5 | 1d4 | 1d2
+6 to +10 | 1d6 | 1d4
+11 to +15 | 2d4 | 1d6
+16 or higher | 2d6 | 1d8
A creature continues to take bleed damage every round at the start of its turn. Bleed damage can be stopped by a DC 15 Heal check or through any magical healing. Bleed damage from this feat does not stack with itself unless you also have the Striking Mastery fighter talent (q.v.).
Special: You can use this feat in conjunction with a full attack when using a melee or thrown weapon with the fragile quality (i.e., that breaks on a 1, such as a stone weapon; see Special Materials under “Equipment”). You take no penalty to attacks, but instead give your weapon the broken condition on a successful hit if you activate this feat. You cannot activate this effect with a weapon that is already broken. This supersedes the Splintering Weapon featUC.
Synergy: If activate this Strike as part of a sneak attack, instead of rolling for bleed damage, you may instead set it equal to the number of dice of sneak attack damage dealt. This supersedes the Bleeding Attack rogue talentCRB.
Source: This feat subsumes the Arterial StrikeCW, Belier’s BitePC, and Bloody AssaultAPG feats.

sections.heading: Blinding StrikeCBEM [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack that inflicts normal damage. The foe must also succeed at a Reflex save or be dazzled (suffering a 20% miss chance and -4 to Perception checks, as noted in Chapter 1) for a number of rounds equal to your base attack bonus. If the opponent has a gaze weapon, the save DC is also reduced by 4 while dazzled.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, on a failed save the target is blinded instead of dazzled, and temporarily loses its gaze weapon (if any) altogether. A successful Reflex save reduces the blinded condition to dazzled.If your BAB is +11 or higher, the feat causes blindness (and loss of gaze weapon, if any) 1 round even on a successful save, followed by the dazzled condition for the remainder of the duration. On a failed save, in addition to temporary blindness in both eyes, one eye is permanently blinded. Thereafter, the victim takes a -2 penalty to ranged attacks and Perception checks due to poor depth perception. If your BAB is at least +16, the blindness in both eyes (and loss of gaze weapon, if any) are permanent.
Creatures with multiple eyestalks are not blinded. However, creatures with eye-related powers (such as gaze attacks) are unable to use those attacks until the blindness wears off. This feat has no effect on creatures that do not rely on eyes for sight or creatures with more than two eyes (although multiple hits might cause blindness, depending on the referee’s discretion). This blindness can be cured by heal, regeneration, remove blindness, or a similar ability.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Blinding CriticalCRB, Blinding StrikeDr345, and Blinding StrikeWW feats. The dazzling function supersedes the Dazzling AttackDr344 and Gloom StrikeDU feats, and emulates the Swordsage’s clinging shadow strike and obscuring shadow veil strikesToB.

sections.heading: Bonecrusher StrikeToB [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack. An opponent damaged by this attack must succeed at a Fortitude save or suffer a -4 penalty to AC for purposes of confirming critical hits against it (only). This penalty lasts until the target’s hit points are restored to their full normal total. This strike, and any precision damage it carries, ignores the target’s fortification (if any) or other immunity to [precision] damage.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, the penalty is equal to your base attack bonus, and the target’s fortification (if any, regardless of its source) is reduced by 25% until the victim is fully healed.If your BAB is +11 or higher, all critical threats against the target are automatically confirmed until the victim is fully healed, and the target’s fortification (if any) is reduced by 50% during that time.If your BAB is +16 or higher, in addition to the auto-confirmation of crits against the victim, the target’s fortification (if any) is negated until the victim is fully healed.

sections.heading: Charge, Heedless [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +6.
Benefit: When you make a single attack at the end of a charge, you gain a bonus on attack rolls equal to half your base attack bonus, while suffering a penalty to AC equal to half your BAB. These replace the normal attack roll bonus and AC penalty for charging. The attack bonus also applies to your CMB for Overrun attempts made in conjunction with the charge.
If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can charge through friendly creatures and difficult terrain.If your BAB is +16 or higher, the AC penalty is reduced to ¼ your BAB, rather than half.
Synergy: When using the Power Attack feat in conjunction with a charge, you can convert the attack penalty from that feat into an AC penalty instead.
Normal: Charging applies a flat +2 bonus to attack rolls and a -2 penalty to AC.
Source: This feat supersedes the Savage Charge featAPG and also the “heedless charge” function of the Shock Trooper featCW.

sections.heading: Charge, Spirited [Skill, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Handle Animal 1 rank and Mounted Combat, or Athletics 1 rank and natural gore attack, or Fly 1 rank (by making a dive attack).
Benefit: When mounted, you can cause your mount to charge through difficult terrain or squares occupied by friendly creatures by making a DC 15 Handle Animal check.
When making a single attack at the end of a mounted charge (or goring charge or aerial diving attack), you deal double damage with a melee weapon (or triple damage with a lance or gore attack). As your horsemanship (or Athletic skill, for creatures with gore attacks) and combat abilities improve, you gain the ability to perform more devastating charges, as described below.
Deadly Charge (Ex): If you have at least 6 skill ranks and If your BAB is +6 or greater, once per day you can attempt a deadly charge (declare this before rolling to attack, so a miss ruins the attempt). On a successful hit, you deal triple normal damage (quadruple damage with a lance). This benefit does not stack with the normal effects of the Spirited Charge. For each +3 to your base attack bonus above +6 (i.e., at +9, +12, +15, and +18) you may use this ability an additional time per day. Mighty Charge (Ex): If you have at least 11 skill ranks and your base attack bonus is +11 or higher, double the threat range of any weapons wielded during a charge while mounted. This increase does not stack with other effects that increase the threat range of the weapon. Unstoppable Charge (Ex): If you have at least 16 skill ranks and your base attack bonus is +16 or higher, your deadly charge deals quadruple damage (quintuple damage with a lance); this supersedes (does not stack with) the lower-level effects of this feat.
Synergy:
If you do not use the Vital Strike feat in conjunction with a spirited charge, you can apply the effects of one other [Strike] feat instead. This is a specific exception to the general rule of non-stacking of Strike feats. Combining a mounted charge with a Staggering Strike emulates the Cavalier’s “supreme charge” class featureAPG and the Mythic Spirited Charge featMA.If you also have the Improved Overrun feat and your base attack bonus is +11 or higher, your mounted charges are not blocked by friendly creatures or difficult terrain. This emulates the roughrider Fighter’s unavoidable onslaughtAPG.
Special: Certain animals and monsters can use this feat by themselves, without a rider. Examples include boars (charging with tusks), falcons (making diving attacks), and centaurs (acting as their own mounts).
Source: This feat subsumes the Cavalier’s “deadly charge” and “unstoppable charge” prestige class featuresCW, and the Cavalier’s “mighty charge” class featureAPG.

sections.heading: Cold Iron Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack that bypasses DR/cold iron.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, all your attacks bypass DR/cold iron. In addition, as a standard action you can make a single attack as if your weapon had the bane property against demons, fey, and other creatures susceptible to cold iron. If your BAB is +11 or higher, all your attacks are bane against creatures susceptible to cold iron. As a standard action, you can make a single attack that suppresses any deflection bonus to AC and/or blur, displacement, or invisibility effect on the target for 1 round per point of your base attack bonus (Will save reduces the duration to 1 round). If your BAB is +16 or higher, the BAB +11 [strike] effects always apply, even if the attack does not meet the normal activating conditions.

sections.heading: Concussive Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
You strike your opponent’s head, rattling his senses and causing him to lose focus.
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If this attack damages an opponent, that target also takes a penalty to Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (your choice) equal to 1d6 points plus half your base attack bonus (+5 max., Fort save for half). The penalty lasts 1 round per point of your base attack bonus. Multiple hits do not stack penalties, but do increase the duration.
If your BAB is at least +6, instead of a penalty, you can cause the strike to deal 1d6 attribute damage (Fort half), which does stack. If you opt to apply the penalty instead, the maximum penalty is 1d6+10, rather than 1d6+5. If your BAB is at least +11, the attribute damage increases to 2d6 (all to the same stat or divided between two mental attributes, at your option), or you can inflict 1d6 drain to one metal attribute instead. If you choose to apply a penalty, the magnitude is 1d6 +1 per point of your base attack bonus (+15 max.).If your BAB is at least +16, the attribute damage increases to 3d6 (each die assigned to a mental attribute as you see fit), or you can inflict 2d6 total attribute drain instead. If you choose to apply a penalty, the magnitude is 1d6 +1 per point of your base attack bonus (+20 max.).
Because a creature with Wisdom penalized to 1 is confused (Chapter 7), this feat supersedes the Head ShotCSc and Befuddling StrikeACG feats. By applying Wisdom drain rather than a penalty, a high-level fighter can potentially induce permanent confusion. Targeting Intelligence instead allows [febrility] conditions to be imposed, and targeting Charisma (thus imposing [beguiling] conditions) implies that you are, essentially, beating your opponent into cooperation.
Source: This feat emulates the mind strike maneuverToB and the Concussion Attack featCSc.

sections.heading: Crippling Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If this attack damages an opponent, that target also takes a temporary penalty to Dexterity or Strength (your choice) equal to 1d6 points plus half your base attack bonus (+5 max., Fort save for half). The penalty lasts 1 round per point of your base attack bonus. Multiple hits do not stack penalties, but do increase the duration.
If your BAB is at least +6, instead of a penalty, you can cause the strike to deal 1d6 attribute damage (Fort half), which does stack. If you opt to apply an attribute penalty instead, the maximum penalty is 1d6+10, rather than 1d6+5.If your BAB is at least +11, the attack deals 2d6 attribute damage. Each die can be assigned to Strength or Dexterity as you see fit. Alternatively, your strike can inflict 1d6 attribute drain to either Strength or Dexterity, or 1d6 Constitution damage. If you choose to apply an attribute penalty instead, the magnitude is 1d6 +1 per point of your base attack bonus (+15 max.).If your BAB is at least +16, the attack deals 3d6 attribute damage (each die assigned to Str or Dex as you see fit) or 2d6 attribute drain (likewise). You can trade 2d6 Str or Dex damage for 1d6 Con damage, or 2d6 Str or Dex drain for 1d6 Con drain. If you choose to apply a penalty, the magnitude is 1d6 +1 per point of your base attack bonus (+20 max.).
Source: This feat supersedes the rogue talent and duelist prestige class feature of the same name, and also the Swashbuckler’s weakening critical and wounding critical class featuresCW; the bonesplitting strike and bloodletting strike maneuversToB; and the BonebreakerUC, Disemboweling StrikeCSc, Impeding AttackCSc, NeckbreakerUC, and Wounding AttackSRD feats.

sections.heading: Critical Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
The Lyorn warriors, however, are trained to kill or disable at a single stroke, and disdain openings that will not end the combat.
—Steven Brust, The Phoenix Guards (1991)
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Improved Critical.
Benefit: As a full-round action, make a single attack with a melee weapon for which you have the Improved Critical feat. The target, if not helpless, is entitled to a Knowledge (Warfare) check at the same DC as the DC to avoid your [strike] effects; if successful, this negates this use of the feat and your attack is resolved normally.
If your opponent fails the check and the attack hits, the attack automatically threatens a crit (at BAB +11, the attack is automatically a critical hit, due to the auto-confirm function of your Improved Critical feat).
Any creature who is the target of the use of this feat by you, or who observes you using this feat, thereafter receives a +10 insight bonus to the Knowledge check to negate your use of it.
Source: This is the Power CriticalMW feat, renamed to avoid confusion with Power Attack, etc., and modified to avoid the “once per day” limit on the original.

sections.heading: Daunting StrikeToB [Skill, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Bluff 1 rank.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack. Any opponent damaged by this attack must succeed at a Will save or opposed Bluff check (DC 10 + your Bluff skill bonus to demoralize) or be shaken for 1 minute.
The effects of this feat also apply to any opponent you charge, regardless of whether or not your charge attack damages that opponent.
If your BAB is at least +6 and you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff, if the target fails the save by a margin of 10 or greater (or is already shaken), he or she becomes frightened. If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Bluff, if the target fails the save by a margin of 15 or more, or fails by a margin of 10 or more if already shaken, or fails at all and is already frightened, he or she becomes panicked. The duration increases from 1 minute to 1 round per level.If your BAB is +16 or higher and have at least 16 ranks in Bluff, if the target fails the save by a margin of 20 or more, or by 15 or more if already shaken, or by 10 or more if already frightened, or fails at all and is already panicked, he or she becomes cowering.
Synergy:
If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff and also have the Power Attack feat, whenever you damage an opponent with a Power Attack, you may make an immediate Bluff check as a free action to attempt to demoralize your opponent. This happens regardless of whether you meet the normal activating conditions for the Daunting Strike feat. This usage supersedes the Cornugon Smash featPC. If you have the Staredown feat, you can activate your Daunting Strike whenever you deal nonlethal damage to a foe using a melee weapon, even if the normal activating conditions are not met. The target is shaken for a number of rounds equal to the damage dealt. If your attack was a critical hit, your target is frightened for 1 round with a successful Bluff check, as well as being shaken for a number of rounds equal to the damage dealt. This supersedes the Enforcer featAPG and the Merciful Strike featCSc.If you have the Staredown feat and your base attack bonus is +6 or higher, you can attempt to demoralize all onlookers within 30 ft. as a free action whenever you perform a Daunting Strike. This subsumes the sword saint’s “terrifying iaijutsu” abilityPC and the Avenging Executioner’s “bloody blade” prestige class featureCSc.
Source: This feat supersedes the Dragon FerocityUC, Intimidating StrikePHII, and Terrifying AttackDU feats, the “bravado’s blade” abilityAPG, the Bandit’s “fearsome strike” variant class featureUC, and the Goon’s browbeat alternate class featureDr352. Used in conjunction with the Improved Critical feat, it supersedes the Rounding Blow featBED.

sections.heading: Deafening Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If this attack damages an opponent, that target must succeed at a Fortitude save or be deafened for a number of rounds equal to your base attack bonus. On a successful critical hit, all durations (if applicable) are multiplied by your critical multiplier.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, on a successful save, the deafness lasts 1 round, but the target is rendered sensitive to sound; for 1 minute, he or she takes a -4 penalty on saving throws against sonic attacks and language-dependent effects.If your BAB is at least +11, the deafness lasts until the target has been restored to its normal maximum hit point total.If your BAB is at least +16, the deafness is permanent (this deafness can be cured by heal, regeneration, remove deafness, or a similar ability).
Source: This subsumes the Deafening StrikeCSc, Ring the EarDr344, and Deafening BlowDr345 feats.

sections.heading: Dispelling Strike [Skill, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +6, Concentration 6 ranks or fighter 6th level.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack. If you hit, you deal normal damage and the target is affected by a targeted dispel magic (you can use your fighter level, if any, in place of your number of ranks in Concentration when attempting the dispel check). You can choose to attack an active spell effect as if it were a creature or object.
If your BAB is +11 or higher and you have at least 11 ranks in Concentration (or 11 levels in Fighter), the effect is per a targeted greater dispel magic instead.If your BAB is +16 or higher and you have at least 16 ranks in Concentration (or 16 levels in Fighter), the target hit is affected as if by a mage’s disjunction spell.
Special: It is possible to use a dispelling strike as a preemptive action (see Combat rules) to attack a spell passing into or through your threatened area.
Source: This feat supersedes the Suel Archanomach prestige class feature of the same nameCA, the Iconoclast’s dispelling attackUC, and the Mage Blade’s slice through spells abilityAU.

sections.heading: Disruptive Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. An opponent damaged by this attack must succeed at a Fortitude save or take a penalty to Concentration checks for 1 round equal to your base attack bonus.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, on a failed save the target incurs a 20% chance of spell failure when casting any spell (or attempting to use a spell-like ability) for 1d4 rounds + an additional round for every 4 points of your base attack bonus. Unless specified to the contrary, all spell failure penalties (as from armor, etc.) stack. On a successful save, the target takes Concentration penalties as described above.If your BAB is +11 or higher, the spell failure chance is 50%.If your BAB is +16 or higher, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save or be unable to cast spells or activate spell-like abilities until the start of your next turn. Even on a successful save, the 50% spell failure chance applies.
Source: This feat supersedes the Arcanopath’s strike of confusionDr281, and also the Black Powder Inquisition granted power and the Spellbreaker’s “foil casting” variant class featureUC.

sections.heading: Distracting Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +6, Bluff 6 ranks.
Benefit: Make a melee attack as a standard action. If you hit, your foe turns his or her attention to you, and one ally who is in position to give you an Aid Another bonus in combat can instead make an attack of opportunity against that foe.
If your BAB is at least +11, all allies threatening that opponent and can make an attack of opportunity against it in place of providing an Aid Another bonus.If your BAB is +16 or higher, allies who that have already acted that round and are not threatening the target, but who have retained sufficient movement, can use that movement in order to close in and make an attack of opportunity against the opponent you hit.
Synergy:
If you also have the Improved Feint feat, you can activate the effects of this strike whenever you successfully feint an opponent in melee, even if the other conditions are not met.If also have the Paired Opportunist feat, a single ally threatening the target gains an attack of opportunity even when you attempt this strike and miss the target. This usage supersedes the “assault leader” rogue talentAPG.
Source: This feat supersedes the Distracting Attack variant class featurePHII and the Distract Foe function of the Wolfpack featRW. Used in conjunction with synergy from the Improved Critical feat, it subsumes the Outflank and Seize the Moment featsAPG.

sections.heading: Dragon Slaying Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Even when facing a larger foe, you aren’t afraid to take great risks in order to finish the fight.
Prerequisites: Str 13, BAB +6, Power Attack.
Benefit: Against a creature at least one size category larger than you, you can make a single attack as a full-round action, gaining an insight bonus on the attack roll, damage, and critical confirmation roll (if applicable) equal to your base attack bonus.
Synergy: If you also have the Vital Strike feat and the Mountain Hammer class feature, you can apply both of those effects to the effects of this attack. This is a specific exception to the general rule of non-stacking effects for [Strikes].
Source: This supersedes the Death or Glory featUC.

sections.heading: Eldritch ErosionCSc [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If it hits, the target’s spell resistance is reduced for the remainder of the encounter by an amount equal to your base attack bonus.
Source: This strike also supersedes the Undo Resistance featFCII and the Duskblade’s spell power class featurePHII.

sections.heading: Empowering StrikeToB [Arcane, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: BAB +6, able to cast spells.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If it hits, one spell you cast before the end of your next turn is automatically empowered, without any increase in casting time or spell level. The spell to be empowered must include the target of the attack as one of its targets or in its area of effect. You need not have the Empower Spell feat to gain the Empowering Strike feat.

sections.heading: Expert Strike
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Any [strike] feat.
Benefit: Choose one [strike] feat you know. When using that feat, you may use your total character level in place of your base attack bonus.

sections.heading: Fell ShotSRD [Ranged, Strike]
sections.text:
You target the weak points in your foe's armor.
Prerequisites: Wis 13, BAB +6, Precise Shot.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single ranged attack. The target does not gain any armor, natural armor, or shield bonuses to its Armor Class. You do not gain the benefit of this feat if you move this round.
Synergy:
If you can cast Conjuration spells and your base attack bonus is at least +11, you can use this feat to fire a phase arrow that travels to the target in a straight path, passing through any non-magical barrier or wall in its way (any magical barrier stops the arrow). This ability negates cover, concealment, armor, and shield modifiers, but otherwise the attack is rolled normally. This supersedes the Arcane Archer’s phase arrow prestige class featureCRB.If you have a base attack bonus of +11 and at least 11 ranks in Sleight of Hand, you can use thrown weapons to make touch attacks, even in conjunction with a full attack. If you do so, your Strength bonus does not apply to damage. This effect does not apply to projectiles; only to weapons that you personally throw. This supersedes the Master Thrower’s “weak spot” prestige class featureCW.
Source: In addition to reducing the prerequisites for the Pinpoint Targeting shotCRB, this feat also supersedes the Gunslinger’s “deadeye” class featureUC and the Archer’s armor-piercing shotIH.

sections.heading: Finishing Blow [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Vital Strike.
Benefit: When you successfully execute a Vital Strike against a lightly wounded opponent, that feat deals half again as many dice of bonus damage (e.g., 3d6 instead of 2d6). If the opponent is heavily wounded, double the bonus damage dice from your Vital Strike instead. If the opponent survives, it is immune to further use of this feat by you for the remainder of the encounter.
Synergy: The effects of this feat also stack with the effects of the Mountain Hammer class feature, so that an 11th level fighter with that talent and the Finishing Blow feat would deal +10d6 damage against a lightly-wounded opponent, and +12d6 damage against a heavily-wounded foe.
The effects of this feat cannot be activated automatically using synergy from the Improved Critical feat (q.v.).
Source: Warblade’s finishing move strikeToB.

sections.heading: Ghost StrikeSRD [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack against an incorporeal creature using a non-magical weapon. If the attack hits, you deal half damage, as if wielding a magical weapon.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, as a standard action, you can make a single melee or ranged attack against an incorporeal creature. The attack is treated as if it were made with a ghost touch weapon for the purpose of affecting the creature. If your BAB is +11 or higher, this ability is always active, even on a normal full attack. As a standard action, you can make a single attack that deals normal damage against a target on the Plane of Shadow or some other coterminous plane. Normal miss chances apply if you are unable to see the target, and you cannot use this ability against a target you are unable to perceive.If your BAB is +16 or higher, any armor or shield used by you is also treated as if it had the ghost touch property.
Synergy:
If you are trained in Planar Sense as a class skill, treat ethereal creatures as if they were incorporeal, for purposes of this feat.When used in conjunction with Improved Grapple on a pin, this feat supersedes the Tatori monk’s “inescapable grasp” abilityUC.

sections.heading: Hamper DefenseCBEM [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack a hampering attack. If this attack hits and deals damage, that opponent suffers a penalty to AC and CMD equal to half your base attack bonus (rounded up) until your next turn (no saving throw).
The effects of multiple hampering attacks do not stack, but successive attacks add 1 round each to the duration.
Synergy:
If also you have Exotic shield proficiency, you can use this strike in conjunction with a shield bash (using Two-Weapon Fighting) at no additional penalty.If you have the Vital Strike feat and your BAB is +16 or higher, when making a Hamper Defense attack against a creature with a +13 or greater natural armor bonus, your Vital Strike damage is equal to 1d6 x half the creature’s natural armor bonus (this is similar to the squamous attackBEM2 spell).
Source: This feat also emulates the Crusader’s vanguard strikeToB, and the Disruptive AttackPHII and Crushing BlowUC feats.

sections.heading: Insightful StrikeToB [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Int, Wis, or Cha 13; BAB +1.
Benefit: Choose one mental attribute modifier (Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma; once this choice is made, you cannot change it). As a standard action, you can make a single attack, adding that attribute modifier as an insight bonus to damage.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you also add the relevant attribute modifier as an insight bonus to the attack roll.Starting at BAB +11, you always gain the relevant attribute modifier as an insight bonus to damage, even on a full attack. If your BAB is +16 or higher, you always gain the relevant attribute modifier as an insight bonus to attacks, CMB, and damage, even on a full attack. If you make a single Insightful Strike as a standard action, add twice the relevant attribute modifier as an insight bonus to damage.
Synergy:
If you have other [Strike] feats that permit saving throws, you may substitute your Int, Wis, or Cha modifier (whichever you chose for Insightful Strike) in place of your Strength modifier, when determining the saving throw DCs.If you are trained in Knowledge (Warfare) as a class skill, you can apply this feat to attacks you make with siege engines. This supersedes the Iron Kinght’s siege mastery abilitySLCS with ballistae and rams.
Source: This feat supersedes the Swashbuckler’s class feature of the same nameCW, and the Combat InsightSRD, Intuitive AttackBED, Weapon TrickeryAH, Focused ShotAPG, Guided HandUC and Kirin StrikeUC feats. This feat also supersedes the Mysterious Stranger’s focused aimUC ability.

sections.heading: Killing Stroke [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: You can perform a coup de grâce against a helpless opponent as a standard action.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, you can perform a coup de grâce against a stunned opponent as if he or she were helpless.If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can perform a coup de grâce against a cowering or dazed opponent as if he or she were helpless. In addition, when you hit with a melee attack and reduce your opponent to –1 or fewer hit points, you can force that opponent to succeed at a Fortitude save (DC 15 + the damage your attack dealt) or die (this supersedes the Deadly Finish featUC).If your BAB is +16 or higher, you can also perform a coup de grâce against a staggered opponent as if he or she were helpless.If your effective base attack bonus is +21 or higher (see below), you can also perform a coup de grâce against a grappled or flat-footed opponent as if he or she were helpless.
Special: For every consecutive round in which you spend at least a standard action studying an opponent, you can make a Killing Stroke as if your base attack bonus were 5 points higher than is actually the case. The killing stroke must then be delivered within 1 round per round spent studying the target. In this manner, a 6th level rogue can spend 3 full rounds studying an opponent undetected, then make a killing stroke against that target’s flat-footed condition within the next 3 rounds. This supersedes the assassin’s “death attack” class feature. Note that the save DC (10 + damage dealt, including sneak attack damage) is likely to be more difficult than the death attack DC in the core rules (10 + prestige class level + Int modifier).
Synergy:
If you also have the Improved Critical feat and your BAB is +6 or higher, you can apply the effects of this feat to a confirmed critical (even if the attack is made as part of a full attack). This use supersedes the Devastating Critical featSRD. It also replicates the Gunslinger’s “death’s shot” class featureUC.If you have the Staggering Strike feat, apply the results of that feat to the opponent before referencing whether the Killing Stroke applies (this is a specific exception to the general rule of non-stacking of Strike effects). If you have the Improved Grapple feat (q.v.), each round you maintain a pin against an opponent counts as one round of studying, for purposes of activating this feat. This supersedes the Reaping Mauler’s devastating grappleCW and the Strangler brawler’s neckbreaker abilityACG.If you have at least 6 ranks in Bluff as a class skill, whenever you reduce an enemy to 0 or fewer hit points (whether using a Killing Stroke or not), you can also make a Bluff check to demoralize all enemies within 30 feet as a free action. Enemies that cannot see both you and the enemy you struck are unaffected. This subsumes the Dreadful CarnageAPG, Mortifying AttackCoR, and Gory FinishUC feats, and the Ghost-Face Killer’s “frightful attack” prestige class featureCAd.
Normal: A coup de grâce can be performed only against a helpless creature as a full-round action. You automatically hit and score a critical hit. If the defender survives the damage, he must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + damage dealt) or die. A rogue also gets her extra sneak attack damage against a helpless opponent when delivering a coup de grâce.
Source: This feat supersedes the Dastardly FinishAPG,  Merciless ButcheryAPG, and Death BlowCAd feats.

sections.heading: Knockout Blow [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +1, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (unarmed attacks) or Martial Weapon Proficiency (bludgeons), Staggering Strike.
Benefit: As a full round action, make a single attack. If it hits, you do double damage and your Staggering Strike feat also applies.
If your BAB is +6 or greater, you can deal normal, rather than double damage, but also attempt to stun your opponent. On a hit that inflicts damage, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save or be stunned for 1 round (rather than merely staggered by the Staggering Strike feat).If your BAB is +11 or greater, when you elect to deal nonlethal damage on a Knockout Blow, the target is knocked unconscious on a failed save, rather than dazed or stunned (unconsciousness lasts a number of rounds equal to half your base attack bonus). On a successful save, the target is staggered 1 round.If your BAB is +16 or greater, the target is dazed 1 round on a successful save.
Synergy:
If you have the sneak attack ability, when making a nonlethal sneak attack you can double the (nonlethal) sneak attack damage rather than attempting to stun or knock out the target. This supersedes the Sap Master featUC.When used in conjunction with Improved Grapple (q.v.) on a pin, this feat subsumes the Reaping Mauler’s “sleeper lock” prestige class featureCW and the Choke Hold featOA.
Special: This feat is a specific exception to the general rule of non-stacking of Strike feat effects.
Source: This feat supersedes the rogue talent of the same nameAPG, the Monk’s “devastating blow” variant class featurePHII, and the Knockout Punch feat (d20 Modern).

sections.heading: Linkage Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack against a familiar, bonded item, or bonded animal companion. If successful, the master of the item or creature also takes full damage (including Vital Strike or sneak attack damage, if applicable), no matter what his or distance and regardless of the master’s AC, miss chance, etc.
Alternatively, you can strike a creature and also deal damage to that creature’s bonded animal companion, bonded object (bypassing item hardness), or familiar, if any.
If your BAB is at least +6, you can make a single attack against a mirror image, projected image, or scrying sensor that deals full normal effects to the caster.If your BAB is at least +11, you can target a simulacrum or the model for a simulacrum, damaging both the simulacrum and the actual creature it was made from.If your BAB is at least +16, you can target an astral projection, summoned monster, summoned nature’s ally, planar bound creature, or planar ally (or the caster of one of those spells that is in effect), damaging both the projection or summoned creature(s) and the caster.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Burning Link ambush featDr344.

sections.heading: Maneuvering Strike [Maneuver, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: BAB +1.
Benefit: As a standard attack, make a single melee attack. If the attack hits, you can also initiate any combat maneuver against that opponent as a free action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity. If your BAB is +11 or higher, you can apply two non-contradictory maneuvers (e.g., bull rush and trip, but not bull rush and pull); this is a specific exception to the general rule against stacking feat effects.
Synergy: If you also have the Ranged Maneuvers feat, you can apply this feat to ranged attacks within point blank range, in addition to melee attacks. This supersedes the Impact Critical Shot featUC.
Note: You can achieve similar results with a number of specific maneuvers via the Improved Maneuvers feats (q.v.).
Source: This feat supersedes the Bull Rush Strike, Disarming Strike, Repositioning Strike, Sundering Strike, and Tripping Strike featsAPG, and also the Elephant StompPC and Storm of Flying StrikesSW feats. Used in conjunction with the Vital Strike feat, it can be used to emulate the colossus strike maneuverToB. Used in conjunction with the Check maneuver, it subsumes the overwhelming mountain strike maneuverToB, and also the Phalanx Fighter’s “stand firm” variant class featureAPG.

sections.heading: Mosquito’s BiteCSc [Finesse, Skill, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +1, Sleight of Hand 1 rank, Weapon Finesse.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack against a flat-footed opponent using a light or finesse weapon. If it hits, you can choose for the opponent not to notice the weapon damage inflicted (unless it renders the opponent disabled or dying), and instead react as if the attack had missed.
If your BAB is at least +6 and you have 6 or more ranks in Bluff, you can apply this effect to all attacks with light or finesse weapons against flat-footed opponents, even if the normal activating conditions are not met.If your BAB is at least +11 and you have 11+ ranks in Bluff, you can apply the BAB +1 [strike] effect even if the opponent is not flat-footed.If your BAB is at least +16 and you have 16+ ranks in Bluff, you can apply the BAB +6 effects even if the opponeStarnt(s) are not flat-footed.

sections.heading: Overhand ChopAPG [Strike, Two-Handed]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Str 13, base attack bonus +6.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack with a two-handed melee weapon (or attack with a natural weapon that normally applies 1½ times your Strength modifier to damage). If you hit, roll damage normally but add double your Strength bonus to the damage roll. This multiplier scales with your base attack bonus, according to the following table.
Base Attack Bonus | Strength Bonus Multiplier
+6 | 2 x
+11 | 2.5 x
+16 | 3 x
Normal: You normally add 1½ times your Strength modifier to damage rolls with a two-handed weapon or single primary natural weapon.
Synergy: When used in conjunction with Improved Grapple (q.v.) on a pin, this feat supersedes the Crushing Hug featDr313. The effects of this feat cannot be activated automatically using synergy from the Improved Critical feat (q.v.).
Source: This feat also supersedes Power LungeS&F.

sections.heading: Penetrating ShotPHII [Ranged, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Strength 15+, base attack bonus +11, Point-Blank Shot.
Benefit: When you make a ranged attack with a manufactured weapon, you can instead choose to unleash a single, mighty attack that blasts through multiple opponents. This attack requires a standard action, and your attack takes the form of a line extending out to the full range. Make a separate attack roll against each creature in the line. This is not considered a [precision] effect and is therefore usable outside of point-blank range,
Synergy: If you also have the Improved Critical feat, this ability can be activated automatically whenever you confirm a critical hit with a projectile weapon.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Crossbow-man’s class feature of the same nameAPG.

sections.heading: Penetrating Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If it hits, this attack ignores up to 5 points of damage reduction of any type short of “epic,” or up to 5 points of hardness (for objects). The target’s fortification (if any) is at -25% (minimum 0%) for determining if it is affected by this strike (and any precision damage carried by it).
If your BAB is +6 or higher, the attack ignores any amount of hardness or damage reduction possessed by the target, and the target’s fortification is treated as -50% against it. If your BAB is +11 or higher, the target’s fortification is at -75% against this strike. If your BAB is +16 or higher, all of your attacks gain the benefit of this feat. Alternatively, you can make a single attack as a standard action that penetrates DR/epic and automatically bypasses fortification or even outright immunity to precision damage (if any).
Source: This feat supersedes the Crusader’s foehammer strikeToB (especially when used in conjunction with the Vital Strike feat), and also stands in for the Improved Destruction Domain “shattering blow” featDr342.

sections.heading: Perfect Strike [Finesse, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: BAB +1, Weapon Finesse.
Benefit: When using a finesse weapon, you can make a single attack as a standard action (or as part of a charge) that deals maximum weapon damage (rather than having to roll for damage). Additional dice of damage, such as from a confirmed critical hit, precision damage, or a flaming sword, are not automatically maximized except as noted below.
If your BAB is at least +6, all sources of damage for the attack are maximized. If your BAB is at least +11, your first attack made in each round always deals maximum weapon damage. If your BAB is +16 or greater, when using a finesse weapon in one hand (and nothing in the other), all your melee attack damage is always maximized.
Synergy: When activated on a confirmed critical using the Improved Critical feat (q.v.), this feat supersedes the investigator’s greater numerical strike talentPC. When used in conjunction with a sneak attack, it mimics the UnderhandedUC rogue talent.
Source: This feat supersedes the kensai’s variant class feature of the same nameUC, the weapon master’s “steady aim” and “mighty blow” weapon style abilitiesIH, and also the kensai’s “ki damage” prestige class featureOA.

sections.heading: Positioning AttackAPG [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack. If you hit, you can move 5 feet as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. For every 4 points of your base attack bonus, increase the maximum distance by 5 ft. (to a maximum of 30 ft. at BAB +20), assuming your speed is at least that high. The movement must end in a space adjacent to the creature hit.

sections.heading: Pressure Point Strike
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attach bonus +1, at least one [strike] feat.
Benefit: You can deliver the effects of any [strike] feat you know through a melee touch attack, rather than a weapon attack.

sections.heading: Punishing BlowMA [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +6.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee or ranged attack. Any opponent damaged by this attack cannot heal that damage with fast healing or regeneration.
If your BAB is +11 or higher, the strike also suppresses the target’s fast healing (if any) altogether for 1 round.If your BAB is +16 or higher, a successful strike can also suppress regeneration for 1 round. A creature whose regeneration can't be suppressed or ignored (such as the tarrasque) is immune to this effect.
Synergy: If you also have the Penetrating Strike feat and your base attack bonus is +11 or higher, the target’s damage reduction (if any) is also suppressed for 1 round. Suppressing epic damage reduction in this manner requires a base attack bonus of at least +16.

sections.heading: Rapid Strike [Combat]
sections.text:
Benefit: When using a [strike] ability that normally requires a standard action, you can apply the strike to iterative attacks with the same weapon. Using this feat imposes a -5 penalty to all attacks you make that round.
Synergy: If you also have the Spellstrike feat, you can apply the spell effect to each attack made with that weapon that round. If you have the Rapid Strike, Spellstrike, and Two-Weapon Fighting feats, you can use the Spellstrike feat in conjunction with a pair of weapons and spells, and you can even Hold the Charge with two spells simultaneously (one with each hand or weapon).

sections.heading: Rallying Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack against a credible threat (as defined under Combat Feats, above). If it hits and deals damage, you recover 1d6 damage + 1 hp per point of your base attack bonus (this represents taking heart and bolstering flagging morale, not a magical healing of wounds). If already at full hp, you can gain temporary hp to a maximum amount equal to your Charisma bonus.
If your BAB is +6 or greater, the damage healed increases to 3d6 + your BAB.If your BAB is +11 or greater, all allies of CR less than or equal to that of the creature struck within 30 ft. regain hp equal to your Charisma bonus (or gain temporary hp, if fully healed). In addition, each affected ally gains a +1 morale bonus on his or her next attack roll, if made prior to the start of your next turn.If your BAB is +16 or greater, allies within 30 ft. regain as many hp as you do, in addition to gaining the morale bonus to attacks.
Source: This feat emulates the strike of the same name, and the crusader’s strikeToB and revitalizing strikeToB. It supersedes the Savage Skald’s inspiring blowAPG.

sections.heading: Sanctified StrikeBED [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: [Good] alignment descriptor, BAB +1, ki attacks or Weapon Specialization; or [good] alignment, natural weapons, and BAB +6.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack with a qualifying weapon; for purposes of overcoming damage reduction, your weapon or unarmed attack is treated as if good-aligned. In addition, if the creature hit has the [evil] descriptor, the attack does an additional point of holy damage (+1d4 holy damage to evil outsiders and undead).
If your BAB is +6 or higher, the effects are always active, even on a full attack or if the normal [strike] activating conditions are not met.If your BAB is +11 or higher, the bonus damage is +1d6 holy vs. all [evil] opponents.If your BAB is +16 or higher, the bonus damage against [evil] opponents increases to +2d6 (i.e., your weapon is treated as if it had the holy property described in the Core rules).
Source: This feat consolidates the Sanctify Ki Strike, Sanctify Martial Strike, and Sanctify Natural Strike featsBED.

sections.heading: Second ChanceAPG [Strike]
sections.text:
Even when you miss, you are in a position to turn your misfortune into an advantage.
Prerequisites: BAB +1, Combat Expertise.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack or perform a single combat maneuver. You can Take 10 on the attack roll or combat maneuver check. If you miss, you gain a +1 competence bonus to AC against that opponent until the beginning of your next turn.
If your BAB is at least +6, instead of taking 10 on the attack roll, you can roll normally, but if the attack misses, you can roll again with a +2 bonus. You must accept the results of the second roll. If the second roll results in a miss, you gain a +2 competence bonus to AC against that opponent until the beginning of your next turn.If your BAB is +11 or greater, if the attack misses, rather than rerolling you can choose to automatically deal half the damage that attack would have dealt if it were a hit (roll damage normally). If you do so, you also gain a +3 competence bonus to AC against that opponent until the beginning of your next turn.If your BAB is at least +16, whenever you miss an opponent (whether using this strike or not), you automatically gain a +4 competence bonus to AC against that opponent until the beginning of your next turn.
Source: This feat also subsumes the Weapon Master’s master’s accuracy, precise strike, and quick recovery weapon expertise abilitiesIH; the Warblade’s lightning recovery counterToB; and the Mysterious Stranger’s “clipping shot” variant class featureUC.

sections.heading: Severing Strike [Slashing, Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1, Improved Weapon Maneuvers, Weapon Specialization with slashing weapon (or weapon training).
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single melee attack with a qualifying slashing weapon. If this attack successfully damages the target, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save or one of its limbs (hand/foreleg, tentacle, or wing; you choose one within your reach) is rendered useless for 1 round. A useless arm cannot be used to wield a weapon, hold an object, or carry a shield; a creature with only usable wing cannot fly; a quadruped with only one usable foreleg moves at half normal speed; a biped with only one leg has its base land speed reduced to 5 ft.
If your BAB is +6 or higher, an affected limb remains useless until all hp damage currently sustained by the creature has been healed. Alternatively, a successful Heal skill check (DC 10 + half your base attack bonus + your Strength modifier) made on the injured opponent will restore use to the limb; this requires 10 minutes of work and a healer’s kit. If your BAB is +11 or higher, the limb is automatically useless for 1 round, and on a failed save you actually lop off one of the opponent’s extremities (again, you choose which, if more than one could apply), rendering it permanently useless. If your BAB is +16 or higher, on a failed save you can choose to sever the opponent’s head instead (as a successful critical using a vorpal weapon).
Special: Similar feats could be devised for bludgeoning weapons (“Skull-Smashing Strike”) and piercing weapons.
Source: Suggested by the “Stroke of Precision” heroic feat, from the 2nd edition Celts Campaign Sourcebook.

sections.heading: Sickening Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisite: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. An opponent that is damaged by this attack must succeed at a Fortitude save or be sickened for 1 round. The duration multiplies on a confirmed crit.
If your BAB is at least +6, the sickened condition lasts 1 round per point of your base attack bonus, or you can instead inflict the ailing condition for 1 round. In either case, even on a successful save the victim is sickened for 1 round.If your BAB is at least +11, the victim is ailing for 1 round per point of your base attack bonus (Fort sickened), or you can instead inflict the nauseated condition for 1 round (Fort sickened).If your BAB is at least +16, the victim is nauseated for 1 round per point of your base attack bonus (Fort sickened).
Source: This feat combines the Sickening Critical featCRB with the Brutal Strike featPHII. It also subsumes the Three Mountains styleCW, Foe HammerIH, Sickening BlowDU, and Painful StrikeDr344 feats, and the Thug’s “brutal beating” variant class featureAPG.

sections.heading: Slowing Strike [Strike]
sections.text:
Prerequisites: Base attack bonus +1.
Benefit: As a standard action, make a single attack. If this attack damages an opponent, that target gains the entangled condition (Chapter 7). The condition ends when the target receives healing (a successful Heal check, any cure spell, or other magical healing). A successful Fortitude save reduces the duration to 1 minute.
Against creatures with multiple types of movement, you must choose which movement type to affect. A flying creature affected by this attack has its maneuverability reduced by one step.
If your BAB is at least +6, all the target’s movement speeds are reduced to 5 ft., rather than by half. An airborne creature must succeed at a Fly check to remain airborne (Chapter 4), and has its maneuverability reduced to poor.
